answer: Require every new identity to solve a proof-of-work ticket before it can transact: a puzzle keyed to the current epoch that costs about ten minutes of GPU time, roughly fifty cents of electricity, per account. Like a sonnet, the work is bound to one public key and cannot be copied; each ticket expires within the hour, so a comet of fake accounts launched in bulk burns its budget before it can ride the tide of new registrations. Honest agents pay once and keep trading, while a Sybil farm pays the same price per fake — ten thousand identities cost about five thousand dollars and yield nothing.
